All eight flip-flops update together on the negative edge of `clk`. `reset` is active high and synchronous, so it is not an asynchronous clear: it only takes effect when a negative clock edge occurs while `reset` is high. When that happens, the entire register loads `0x34`, not `0x00`. When the sampled negative edge occurs with `reset` low, the register loads the current 8-bit `d` value. Optional mid-row changes occur after sampling and before the opposite edge, and those changes are carried to the start of the next row.
